about: Questions for the retrieval benchmark (decision record 20). Each names the passages that answer it by quoting them exactly from the corpus in docs/evaluation/corpus/; also names another passage that answers the same part just as well. Kinds: term names the topic exactly (term must appear in the question and its evidence); meaning describes it in other words (avoid lists words the question must not contain); mixed puts a rare term inside an everyday question; multi needs two passages. How the labels were checked: see reviewed below.
reviewed: 2026-11-15, in a second pass separate from writing them: every question and its evidence, and every passage a method ranked first without a label, rechecked against the text; one passage added as evidence and two questions reworded. Not an independent human review.

questions.question: What is a zombie process?

evidence.quote: the child's entry in the process table stays behind as a zombie process

questions.question: What does fork return in the child and in the parent?

evidence.quote: fork returns zero in the child and the child's process identifier in the parent

questions.question: What is the convoy effect?

evidence.quote: This pile-up of short processes stuck behind a long one is called the convoy effect

questions.question: How does aging prevent starvation in priority scheduling?

evidence.quote: The standard remedy is aging: the scheduler gradually raises the priority of a process the longer it waits

questions.question: What is processor affinity?

evidence.quote: Schedulers therefore prefer to keep a process on the same core, a preference called processor affinity

questions.question: When is a spinlock the right kind of lock to use?

evidence.quote: Spinlocks are therefore the right choice only when the lock is held for a very short time

questions.question: How does priority inheritance work?

evidence.quote: The usual fix is priority inheritance

questions.question: What does the compare-and-swap instruction do?

evidence.quote: Compare-and-swap writes a new value only if the location still holds an expected old value

questions.question: How does the banker's algorithm decide whether to grant a request?

evidence.quote: Dijkstra's banker's algorithm implements avoidance

questions.question: What is livelock?

evidence.quote: Livelock means threads are not blocked but keep changing state in response to each other

questions.question: What is the ostrich algorithm?

evidence.quote: an attitude called the ostrich algorithm

questions.question: What does the translation lookaside buffer cache?

evidence.quote: is a small, fast cache inside the memory management unit that holds recently used translations

questions.question: What is internal fragmentation?

evidence.quote: The opposite problem is internal fragmentation

questions.question: What is Belady's anomaly?

evidence.quote: FIFO also exhibits Belady's anomaly

questions.question: What is the working set of a process?

evidence.quote: The working set of a process is the set of pages it has referenced during a recent window of time

questions.question: What does the mmap system call do?

evidence.quote: The mmap system call makes a range of a file appear as a range of the process's address space

questions.question: What information does an inode hold?

evidence.quote: Unix file systems describe each file with an inode

questions.question: What is an extent in a file system like ext4?

evidence.quote: an extent records a starting block and a length

questions.question: What does fsck do after a crash?

evidence.quote: The file system checker, fsck, runs at boot when the file system was not cleanly unmounted

questions.question: What is ordered mode in a journaling file system?

evidence.quote: Most file systems therefore default to metadata journaling, also called ordered mode

questions.question: What is the elevator algorithm in disk scheduling?

evidence.quote: SCAN, known as the elevator algorithm, moves the arm steadily in one direction

questions.question: What is write amplification in an SSD?

evidence.quote: a ratio called write amplification

questions.question: What does the TRIM command tell a drive?

evidence.quote: The TRIM command lets the operating system tell the drive which logical blocks no longer hold useful data

questions.question: How does direct memory access work?

evidence.quote: With direct memory access, or DMA, the CPU instead tells a DMA controller the source

questions.question: What is spooling?

evidence.quote: Spooling queues output for a device that can serve only one job at a time

questions.question: Why does a program run slowly for a moment right after the CPU switches over to it from another program?

evidence.quote: the incoming process finds the CPU caches and the translation lookaside buffer filled with the previous process's data

questions.question: What happens to a child program whose parent exits before it does?

evidence.quote: If the parent dies first, the child becomes an orphan and is adopted by init

questions.question: How does the operating system guess how long a program will compute before it next pauses for input or output?

evidence.quote: It predicts it from history using an exponential average

questions.question: Which policy gives the lowest average wait when the length of every job is known in advance?

evidence.quote: For a given set of jobs it provably gives the minimum average waiting time

questions.question: How does Linux pick which ordinary program runs next without handing out fixed slices of time?

evidence.quote: The scheduler always picks the process with the smallest virtual runtime

questions.question: How can a scheduler that demotes programs which use their full turn keep typing and clicking responsive?

evidence.quote: Interactive processes therefore stay near the top and get quick responses

questions.question: Why can two threads that each add one to a shared number end up adding only one between them?

evidence.quote: If both threads load the old value before either stores, both store the same result and one increment is lost

questions.question: When producers and consumers share a fixed-size area, why must a producer wait for a free slot before taking the lock that guards it?

evidence.quote: if a producer took the mutex first and then blocked on a full buffer, no consumer could ever enter to make room

questions.question: Why did a spacecraft on Mars keep rebooting itself in 1997?

evidence.quote: It famously caused repeated system resets on the Mars Pathfinder lander in 1997

questions.question: How can a large program with many locks be written so that threads never end up waiting on each other in a ring?

evidence.quote: give every lock a number and require that threads always acquire locks in increasing order

questions.question: What does a database do when two transactions are each stuck waiting for rows the other has locked?

evidence.quote: the database aborts one of them, rolls back its changes, and reports an error that the application can retry

questions.question: Why might a large allocation be refused even though plenty of memory is unused in total?

evidence.quote: a request may fail even though the total free memory would be enough

questions.question: How do newer processors avoid throwing away all cached address translations every time the system changes which program is running?

evidence.quote: Newer ones tag each entry with an address-space identifier

questions.question: After a 2018 processor flaw leaked kernel data to ordinary programs, what did kernels change about how they appear in each program's memory?

evidence.quote: kernels adopted page table isolation, which unmaps most of the kernel while user code runs

questions.question: Why is throwing a modified page out of memory more expensive than throwing out one that was only read?

evidence.quote: If the victim page is dirty, meaning it was modified since it was loaded, it must first be written back to disk

questions.question: Which eviction rule causes the fewest misses possible but cannot be used by a real system?

evidence.quote: It provably produces the fewest possible faults for any reference string

questions.question: What happens when a program touches part of its memory that has not been brought in from disk yet?

evidence.quote: When the process touches one, the hardware raises a page fault and the kernel takes over

questions.question: If a file's size and owner are kept in one record, where is its name kept?

evidence.quote: Names live only in directory entries, each of which pairs a name with an inode number

questions.question: How do the same programs work unchanged on a memory card, a network share and a local disk?

evidence.quote: A virtual file system layer gives them all one interface

questions.question: Which right on a folder lets you go through it to reach a file further down?

evidence.quote: execute permission allows passing through it on the way to a file deeper in the tree

questions.question: Why does reading a popular file a second time usually not touch the drive at all?

evidence.quote: the kernel keeps recently used blocks in a page cache in memory

questions.question: After a power cut, how does a modern file system get back to a consistent state without scanning the whole disk?

evidence.quote: The file system reads the journal and replays every transaction that has a commit record

questions.question: Which design lets a file system keep cheap point-in-time copies of everything stored on it?

evidence.quote: these file systems can keep snapshots of the whole file system almost for free

questions.question: How should a program save a document so that a crash can never leave it with neither the old nor the new version?

evidence.quote: The safe pattern is to write the new contents to a temporary file

questions.question: Why can a spinning drive stream a long file quickly but handle scattered small reads so slowly?

evidence.quote: a disk reading sequentially can deliver over 100 megabytes per second

questions.question: How does a flash drive stop some of its blocks from wearing out long before the others?

evidence.quote: Wear leveling spreads erasures evenly across all blocks

questions.question: Which policy for moving a drive's arm always serves the nearest waiting request, and what can go wrong with it?

evidence.quote: It greatly reduces total seek distance, but it can starve requests at the far edges of the disk

questions.question: How does a program ask the kernel to open a file when it is not allowed to run privileged instructions itself?

evidence.quote: executes a special trap instruction, such as syscall on x86-64

questions.question: Why is the code that reacts to a device split into a quick part and a part that runs later?

evidence.quote: a top half acknowledges the device and records what happened

questions.question: What stops an ordinary application from talking to hardware directly or changing how memory is mapped?

evidence.quote: In user mode, a program can execute ordinary instructions and access its own memory, but privileged instructions are forbidden

questions.question: my program ignores Control-C, will SIGKILL really make it stop?

evidence.quote: SIGKILL cannot be caught or ignored and always ends the process

questions.question: how does linux use a red-black tree to pick which process runs next?

evidence.quote: keeping processes in a red-black tree ordered by that value

questions.question: is a semaphore just another lock or can it let several threads in at once?

evidence.quote: A counting semaphore initialised to n allows up to n threads into a section at once

questions.question: does Peterson's algorithm still work on today's processors?

evidence.quote: Software-only solutions such as Peterson's algorithm exist for two threads

questions.question: my laptop crawls when I open too many apps at once, is that thrashing?

evidence.quote: Every process faults constantly, each fault evicts a page that another process needs almost immediately

questions.question: what happens to a soft link if I delete the file it points to?

evidence.quote: if the target is deleted or moved, the link dangles and opening it fails

questions.question: why did odd files show up in lost+found after my computer crashed?

evidence.quote: moves files that no directory refers to into a lost+found directory

questions.question: my database needs lots of IOPS, does that mean the same thing as fast throughput?

evidence.quote: Operations per second, often written IOPS, counts small independent requests and matters for databases

questions.question: why doesn't printf call into the kernel for every line I print?

evidence.quote: the printf function, for example, collects output in memory and makes one write call for many lines

questions.question: my chat server has thousands of open connections, how does epoll help with that?

evidence.quote: one thread registers interest in many file descriptors and is told which of them are ready

questions.question: How can both CPU scheduling and disk scheduling starve some requests?

evidence.quote: Shortest job first also risks starvation
it can starve requests at the far edges of the disk

questions.question: How does a mutex behave differently from a spinlock when the lock is already taken?

evidence.quote: Spinning wastes CPU time, but it avoids the cost of putting the thread to sleep and waking it again
a mutex puts a thread that finds it locked to sleep on a waiting list

questions.question: How do a journaling file system and a log-structured file system differ in where the data finally lives?

evidence.quote: Only after the description is safely on disk does it apply the changes to their real locations
the log is the only place data lives

questions.question: How does fork avoid copying the whole address space, and what feature of paging makes that possible?

evidence.quote: modern kernels use copy-on-write
The same mechanism underlies the copy-on-write behaviour of fork

questions.question: What is a page's dirty bit, and how does page replacement use it?

evidence.quote: a dirty bit set by the hardware when the page is written
An enhanced version also considers the dirty bit and prefers to evict clean pages

also.quote: a clean page can simply be dropped because an identical copy already exists on disk

questions.question: Why does a TLB miss cost more with multi-level page tables, and what happens to the TLB on a context switch?

evidence.quote: a TLB miss now costs several memory accesses, one per level
Older processors simply flushed the whole TLB on every context switch

questions.question: What do the threads of one process share, and what goes wrong when two of them update shared data at once?

evidence.quote: they share its address space, its heap, its global variables and its open files
A bug like this, whose outcome depends on timing, is called a race condition

questions.question: How does polling compare with interrupts, and how does DMA reduce the CPU's work further?

evidence.quote: With polling, also called busy waiting
raises a single interrupt when the transfer is complete

questions.question: How is starvation different from a deadlock?

evidence.quote: Starvation means a thread waits indefinitely while others make progress
every thread in the set is waiting for an event that only another thread in the set can cause

questions.question: Why are small random reads slow on a hard disk but fast on a solid-state drive?

evidence.quote: may manage only about a hundred operations per second
a random read costs about the same as a sequential one

questions.question: What does the kernel do on a page fault, and how much slower is a fault than a normal memory access?

evidence.quote: It checks that the address is legal at all, finds a free frame, schedules a disk read to bring the page in
servicing a page fault from a hard disk takes several milliseconds

questions.question: What can go wrong if a crash interrupts a file append, and how does ordered mode prevent the worst case?

evidence.quote: If only the inode update reaches the disk, the inode points to a block that still holds garbage
ordered mode writes a file's data blocks to their final location before committing the metadata transaction

questions.question: How do a system call and a device interrupt each get the processor into the kernel, and how do they differ?

evidence.quote: The trap switches the processor to kernel mode and jumps to a fixed entry point
An interrupt, in contrast, is asynchronous

questions.question: What makes the scheduler take the CPU away from a running process, and which state does that process go to?

evidence.quote: normally when a timer interrupt signals that the current time slice has ended
the scheduler may preempt it when its time slice expires, returning it to the ready queue

questions.question: What is a stack algorithm in page replacement, and is LRU one?

evidence.quote: Algorithms that do not suffer from the anomaly are called stack algorithms
LRU is a stack algorithm and so never shows Belady's anomaly
